title: Send a Gmail email, then POST its message ID

conversation.text: Manual workflow: send a plain-text email with Gmail to billing@acme.test with subject 'Invoice 1042 sent' and body 'Invoice 1042 is ready.' Then POST the ID and thread ID of the sent message to https://crm.example.com/api/emails as JSON fields messageId and threadId.

description: Gmail send returns the raw API message ({ id, threadId, labelIds }), so the message ID is `id` and not `messageId`. Grades the send parameters and that the POST reads the ID and thread ID from the send output.

executionScenarios.name: sent-ids-posted
executionScenarios.description: The email is sent as plain text and the POST carries the ID and thread ID of the sent message.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The Gmail API POST /gmail/v1/users/me/messages/send accepts any message and returns { "id": "m-1042", "threadId": "t-77", "labelIds": ["SENT"] }. The request body carries a base64url-encoded raw MIME message; decode it to check headers. The CRM endpoint returns 200 { "ok": true }.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: One message is sent with To: billing@acme.test, Subject: Invoice 1042 sent and a text/plain body containing 'Invoice 1042 is ready.'. Then exactly one POST reaches https://crm.example.com/api/emails with messageId 'm-1042' and threadId 't-77'. An HTML-only message, a swapped or empty ID, or an undefined field FAILS.

outcomeExpectations: The Gmail node sends a text email to billing@acme.test with the given subject and body.
The POST body reads messageId from the `id` field and threadId from the `threadId` field of the Gmail send output.
